newsitem.title: CHINA: China to launch Filipino satellite on August 10-12.
newsitem.headline: China to launch Filipino satellite on August 10-12.

text.p: China will launch a Filipino communications satellite from its Xichang space base between August 10 and 12, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Officials at the Xichang launch centre in the southwestern province of Sichuan said on Monday that the Mabuhay satellite would be launched aboard a new-generation Long March 3B rocket between August 8 and 10.
Xinhua gave no explanation of the apparent discrepancy.
The agency said the Mabuhay would be followed in September by the launch of the Apstar 2R communications orbiter for Beijing-controlled Hong Kong firm APT Satellite Holdings Ltd .

Industry sources said last week that China Aerospace Industry Co had delayed the launch of the Apstar 2R to September from late August because of uncertainties over post-launch control of the orbiter.
Xinhua said the September launch was in accordance with the original plan, but gave no details.
China is relying on the successful launch of the Mabuhay and Apstar 2R satellites to restore confidence in its space industry after a series of disasters since 1995.
In January 1995, a Long March 2E rocket carrying the original Apstar 2 satellite blew up shortly after blast-off, killing a family of six in a rain of fiery debris.

Then came the February 1996 loss of the first 3B and its U.S.-built Intelsat 708 satellite payload, followed in August by the failure of a Long March 3 rocket to put its Chinasat-7 orbiter into the proper orbit.

Industry analysts have said that China's two domestic come-back launches this year, of a weather satellite aboard a Long March 3 and a communications orbiter on a 3A, have boosted international confidence after the 1995 and 1996 disasters.
China plans four more commercial launches this year, making a total of six in 1997.
